items.q: Match the mode of inheritance with the affected chain in Alport syndrome — 1) X-linked (80%)  2) Autosomal recessive (15%)  3) Autosomal dominant (5%) … A) α3/α4  B) α3/α4  C) α5
items.exp: Inheritance table: X-linked (80%) affects the α5 chain; AR (15%) and AD (5%) both affect α3/α4. (Book p783)

items.q: The commonest mode of inheritance in Alport syndrome, X-linked, accounts for:
items.exp: X-linked inheritance accounts for 80% of Alport syndrome, affecting the α5 chain, with ESRD by 30 years in males and females as carriers. (Book p783)

items.q: A man with X-linked Alport syndrome reaches end-stage renal disease. According to the table, ESRD occurs:
items.exp: X-linked (80%) Alport syndrome: ESRD by 30 years in males (♂), with females (♀) as carriers. (Book p783)

items.q: In the AR form of Alport syndrome, ESRD occurs by 40 years and affects both females and males.
opts: False — AR Alport causes ESRD only in males by 30 years
False — AR Alport never causes ESRD
True, but AR accounts for 80% of cases
items.exp: AR (15%) affects α3/α4 and causes ESRD by 40 years in both ♀ and ♂. (Book p783)

items.q: Match each Alport inheritance pattern with its features — 1) X-linked (80%)  2) Autosomal recessive (15%)  3) Autosomal dominant (5%) … A) ESRD by 30 years in males; females are carriers  B) Mild disease in females and males  C) ESRD by 40 years in females and males
items.exp: Inheritance table: X-linked (80%, α5) gives ESRD by 30 years in males with females as carriers; AR (15%, α3/α4) gives ESRD by 40 years in both sexes; AD (5%, α3/α4) is mild in both sexes. (Book p783)

items.q: Fill up: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome (5%) produces ______ disease in females and males.
items.exp: AD (5%) Alport syndrome affects α3/α4 and produces mild disease in both females and males. (Book p783)

items.q: Autosomal recessive Alport syndrome accounts for what proportion of cases?
items.exp: Alport inheritance: X-linked 80%, AR 15%, AD 5%. (Book p783)
